results.claim: Complement equivalence and exact endpoint cases. Let F(n,k) count labelled graphs on [n] with vertex-cover number at most k, let N=binom(n,2), and put m=n−k. For 0≤k≤n, F(n,k)=2^N−T(n,m), where T(n,m) is the number of labelled K_m-free graphs. Consequently F(n,n−3)=2^N−T(n,3), with T(n,3) the triangle-free graph count. Also F(n,0)=1; F(n,1)=1+n(2^{n−1}−1)−binom(n,2); F(n,n−2)=2^N−1; and F(n,n−1)=F(n,n)=2^N.
results.proof_sketch: For every graph G, a set C is a vertex cover exactly when V(G)\C is independent. Hence τ(G)=n−α(G), and τ(G)≤k exactly when G has an independent m-set. Complementation turns independent m-sets into K_m subgraphs, proving the identity; for m=0 this uses the standard empty-clique convention. For k=1, every admissible nonempty edge set is a subset of a labelled star. A one-edge graph occurs in two star sums, whereas an admissible graph with at least two edges has a unique common center. Adding the empty graph and correcting the one-edge double count gives the formula. The other endpoint formulas follow from independent sets of sizes two, one, or zero.

results.claim: There is a deterministic exact algorithm using polynomial space and time 2^{q+O(n)}, where q=binom(n,2)−binom(n−k,2)=kn−k(k+1)/2. Therefore the target is achieved whenever k=o(n), including k=O(n/log n).
results.proof_sketch: For every k-subset C⊆[n], generate the 2^q graphs having no edge inside [n]\C. Count a generated graph only when C is its first k-cover in a fixed total order. Every graph with τ≤k has a k-cover by extending a smaller cover, and it is retained exactly once. There are binom(n,k)2^q generated pairs, and canonicality uses at most binom(n,k) polynomial-time cover tests per pair. Thus the time is poly(n)·binom(n,k)^2·2^q=2^{q+O(n)}. A graph mask, subset iterators, and an O(n²)-bit counter give polynomial space. Since q≤nk, the exponent is o(n²) whenever k=o(n).

results.claim: For every fixed k there is a polynomial-time exact algorithm. More explicitly, F(n,k) is computable in time at most poly(n)·sum_{t=0}^k binom(n,t)·2^{binom(t,2)+t}·[2(t+2)]^{2^t−1}.
results.proof_sketch: Count graphs of vertex-cover number exactly t by their lexicographically first minimum cover C. Fix C and H=G[C], and put I=[n]\C. For each nonempty H-independent X⊆C, let U_X contain the vertices of I adjacent to X. Then C is minimum exactly when |U_X|≥|X| for every X. Equality produces the alternative minimum cover (C\X)∪U_X, and every alternative arises this way. In increasing-label lexicographic order, C precedes that cover exactly when min X<min U_X. A DP scans I and, for each X, stores |U_X| capped at |X|+1 and whether U_X contains a label below min X. Each vertex has 2^t neighborhood types. There are at most 2^t−1 coordinates and at most 2(t+2) states per coordinate. Summing over C and the 2^{binom(t,2)} choices of H gives the displayed bound and counts each graph once.

results.claim: Exact first- and second-moment formulas give certified bounds for all parameters. For 1≤m≤n, let q=N−binom(m,2), S1=binom(n,m)2^q, and S2=binom(n,m)·sum_{j=max(0,2m−n)}^m binom(m,j)binom(n−m,m−j)2^{N−2binom(m,2)+binom(j,2)}. Then max{2^q, ceil(S1²/S2)}≤F(n,n−m)≤min{2^N,S1}. In particular, q≤log₂F(n,n−m)≤q+n.
results.proof_sketch: For a graph G, let X(G) be its number of independent m-subsets. Choosing one independent m-set leaves q free edges, so sum_G X(G)=S1. For an ordered pair S,T with |S∩T|=j, independence of both forbids 2binom(m,2)−binom(j,2) distinct edges. For each S, the number of possible T is binom(m,j)binom(n−m,m−j), proving S2=sum_G X(G)^2 without an ordered-versus-unordered factor loss. Since 1_{X>0}≤X, F≤S1. Cauchy–Schwarz gives S1²≤F·S2, and fixing one independent m-set gives F≥2^q. Finally binom(n,m)≤2^n yields the logarithmic bracket.

results.claim: At the triangle-free endpoint, a substantial subclass is exactly countable in polynomial time. Let B_n be the number of labelled bipartite graphs and P_n=sum_{a=0}^n binom(n,a)2^{a(n−a)}. Then B_0=1 and B_n=(P_n−sum_{a=1}^{n−1}binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a})/2. Hence F(n,n−3)≤2^N−B_n is an exact-arithmetic, polynomial-time computable bound.
results.proof_sketch: P_n counts a graph together with an ordered proper two-coloring: choose the first color class and then arbitrary cross edges. A bipartite graph with c connected components is counted 2^c times. The convolution sum over a counts the same weighted objects by assigning every connected component wholly to one of two labelled blocks and selecting a bipartite graph on each block. Thus P_n=sum_{a=0}^n binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a}. Isolating the a=0,n terms gives the recurrence. It performs polynomially many operations on O(n²)-bit integers. Since every bipartite graph is triangle-free, T(n,3)≥B_n; the complement identity then gives the bound.

final_writeup: The full uniform 2^{o(n²)} algorithm remains unresolved here. The main positive result is an exact 2^{kn−k(k+1)/2+O(n)} algorithm, which settles every asymptotic regime k=o(n), together with a polynomial-time algorithm for each fixed k. The uncovered range includes k=n−3, which is already equivalent to exact enumeration of labelled triangle-free graphs. The moment formulas and bipartite recurrence provide independently checkable bounds in that range but do not determine the exact count.
